prompts.description: Adaptive endurance training planner and physiological simulator
prompts.text:
Build an interactive adaptive training planner and physiological simulator for four endurance disciplines: triathlon, running, cycling, and cross-training (cycling, running, and easy weight training).
The goal is an exceptional visual and functional result, as polished and impressive as a flagship sports-science studio, not a mere technical demo.
Expected result:

* An athlete profile editor accepts physiological baselines—FTP (watts and W/kg), VO2max or recent race time, threshold heart rate, Critical Swim Speed (CSS) pace, weekly training hours, and sessions per week—and automatically computes individualized Coggan power zones, running pace zones, heart rate zones, and swim pace zones.
* A multi-week periodized plan generator structures mesocycles (Base, Build, Peak, Taper, plus recovery weeks) from start date to race day, tailored to the chosen discipline (triathlon, running, cycling, or cross-training combining cycling, running, and foundational weight training) while respecting weekly session and hour budgets.
* An interactive Performance Management Chart models daily Training Stress Score (TSS), Chronic Training Load (CTL, 42-day EWMA), Acute Training Load (ATL, 7-day EWMA), and Training Stress Balance (TSB = CTL - ATL) from start date to race day.
* Every workout renders as a visual interval block profile (warm-up, work intervals at exact target watts, pace, or heart rate, recovery valleys, cool-down, or structured strength sets) with calendar (.ics) and structured workout (.zwo) export.
* Live plan adaptation lets the athlete mark sessions as skipped, shortened, or over-reached, or simulate illness and changed weekly availability; the engine dynamically recalibrates the remaining plan to cap weekly ramp rate and peak on race day, overlaying the original and adapted CTL/ATL/TSB curves.

Reference physiological models:

* Banister impulse-response & Performance Management Chart: CTL_t = CTL_{t-1} + (TSS_t - CTL_{t-1}) / 42, ATL_t = ATL_{t-1} + (TSS_t - ATL_{t-1}) / 7, TSB_t = CTL_t - ATL_t
* Coggan 7-zone cycling power & stress: IF = NP / FTP, TSS = (seconds * NP * IF) / (FTP * 3600) * 100
* Daniels VDOT running zones & rTSS: Easy, Marathon, Threshold, Interval, and Repetition paces derived from VDOT / recent race performance, with running stress scaled against threshold pace
* Critical Swim Speed (CSS): CSS (m/s) = (400 - 200) / (T_400 - T_200) and swim stress sTSS = IF^3 * hours * 100

prompts.description: French electricity system observatory and carbon flow simulator
prompts.text:
Build an interactive observatory and grid stress-test simulator of the French electricity system, mapping regional generation, power plants, cross-border flows, and carbon intensity.
The goal is an exceptional visual result, as clear, authoritative and impressive as a national grid control room and energy atlas, not a mere technical demo.
Expected result:

* A map of metropolitan France shows the 12 administrative regions colored by net electrical balance (net exporter vs. net importer), with animated cross-border interconnections (UK, Belgium, Germany, Switzerland, Italy, Spain) sized by physical flow.
* Major power plants and storage facilities are plotted across the country, sized by installed capacity (MW) and colored by technology (nuclear, hydro, pumped storage, wind, solar, thermal, bioenergy).
* A legend and technology filter list each generation source with its live output (MW), share of the mix (%), and capacity factor. Clicking a source or region isolates and inspects its profile.
* A high-resolution timeline scrubber lets the viewer step through a full year (with presets for winter peak demand and summer solar peak), displaying stacked generation by source against total consumption and live carbon intensity (gCO2eq/kWh).
* An interactive grid stress-test simulator lets the viewer vary nuclear fleet availability (%), wind and solar load factors, and winter temperature anomaly (°C thermosensitivity) to observe real-time adequacy margin, import needs, and load-shedding thresholds.
* Selecting any region opens a detailed breakdown of its generation fleet, local demand, self-sufficiency ratio, and net regional transfers.

Available data sources (Open Licence / Etalab):

* ODRE (RTE), "Données éCO2mix nationales consolidées et définitives" (national generation by source, consumption, cross-border flows and carbon intensity): https://odre.opendatasoft.com/explore/dataset/eco2mix-national-cons-def
* ODRE (RTE), "Données éCO2mix nationales temps réel" (real-time national electricity mix and carbon intensity): https://odre.opendatasoft.com/explore/dataset/eco2mix-national-tr
* ODRE (RTE), "Données éCO2mix régionales consolidées et définitives" (regional generation, consumption and flows across the 12 metropolitan regions): https://odre.opendatasoft.com/explore/dataset/eco2mix-regional-cons-def
* ODRE, "Registre national des installations de production et de stockage d'électricité" (power plants and storage facilities with technology, commune and installed capacity): https://odre.opendatasoft.com/explore/dataset/registre-national-installation-production-stockage-electricite-agrege
* Etalab / data.gouv.fr, "Contours administratifs – Régions" (French regional boundaries GeoJSON): https://etalab-datasets.geo.data.gouv.fr/contours-administratifs/latest/geojson/regions-100m.geojson

prompts.description: 24-hour French passenger rail network map and accessibility atlas
prompts.text:
Build an interactive 24-hour animated map and accessibility atlas of the French passenger rail network (TGV, Intercités, TER).
The goal is an exceptional visual result, as beautiful and impressive as a national railway control center and transport atlas, not a mere technical demo.
Expected result:

* Smooth 24-hour timeline scrubbing and animation of every scheduled passenger train across metropolitan France, colored and sized by service category (TGV, Intercités, TER), with a legend to filter or highlight each category.
* Interactive station-to-station travel-time accessibility mode: clicking any station computes and colors all reachable stations across France by shortest rail travel time (<1h, 1–2h, 2–3h, 3–5h, >5h), including transfer wait times.
* A daily corridor flow view showing cumulative 24-hour train frequency along each line of the national rail network (RFN), with line weight and luminance scaled by traffic volume.
* Live statistics for the current clock time showing active trains in circulation by category, the 24-hour traffic profile, and the busiest stations.
* Selecting any train or station displays its full stop-by-stop timetable, route path, and scheduled connections.

Available data sources (Open Licence / ODbL):

* transport.data.gouv.fr, "Réseau SNCF TGV, Intercités et TER" (GTFS schedules for TGV, Intercités and TER): https://transport.data.gouv.fr/datasets/horaires-sncf
* SNCF Open Data, "HORAIRES SNCF" (GTFS timetable catalog and archive): https://ressources.data.sncf.com/explore/dataset/horaires-sncf
* SNCF Open Data, "Fichier de formes des lignes du Réseau Ferré National" (RFN rail line geometries): https://ressources.data.sncf.com/explore/dataset/formes-des-lignes-du-rfn

prompts.description: Metropolitan France road accidents collision observatory (BAAC)
prompts.text:
Build an interactive map and collision observatory of road accidents in metropolitan France that reveals who hits whom, where, and under what conditions.
The goal is an exceptional visual result, as clear, insightful and impressive as a flagship data-journalism piece or a great atlas, not a mere technical demo.
Expected result:

* Every geolocated corporeal accident in metropolitan France from the latest validated year (or last 3 years) is mapped and colored by worst injury severity (unharmed, slight injury, hospitalized, killed) or by victim transport mode, joining the four BAAC tables (`caracteristiques`, `lieux`, `vehicules`, `usagers`).
* An interactive "who hits whom" collision matrix cross-tabulates the victim's mode of transport (pedestrian, bicycle, e-scooter/EDPM, motorized two-wheeler, passenger car, heavy vehicle) against the opposing vehicle category in the same accident, including single-vehicle crashes and pedestrians struck by a vehicle. Clicking a cell filters the map and all charts.
* Interactive filters slice accidents by hour of day, day of week, lighting conditions, weather, road category, speed limit, and presence of cycling infrastructure.
* A live summary panel updates with the current map viewport and active filters to show total accidents, fatality and hospitalization rates, victim age distribution, and top collision pairs.
* Selecting an individual accident or local cluster inspects its full relational record: location and road profile, involved vehicles, and every user's role, age, sex, safety equipment, and injury outcome.
* Department boundaries provide geographic context across metropolitan France, with national-to-street zoom and a department ranking by accident rate or severity.

Available data sources (Open Licence / Etalab):

* ONISR, "Bases de données annuelles des accidents corporels de la circulation routière (BAAC)" (`caracteristiques`, `lieux`, `vehicules`, `usagers` CSV tables and codebook): https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/bases-de-donnees-annuelles-des-accidents-corporels-de-la-circulation-routiere-annees-de-2005-a-2024

prompts.description: Paris 1910 3D flood simulator with building ground elevations and river gauges
prompts.text:
Build an interactive 3D flood simulator of Paris that lets the viewer raise the level of the Seine centimeter by centimeter, from its normal level up to and beyond the historic 1910 centennial flood (+8.62 m at the Pont d'Austerlitz).
The goal is an exceptional visual result, as dramatic, clear and impressive as a great interactive atlas or museum exhibit, not a mere technical demo.
Expected result:

* Every building in inner Paris rises from its real ground elevation to its real height along the Seine and across low-lying districts.
* A continuous water-level slider (0 m to +10 m at the Pont d'Austerlitz gauge) with historical flood markers (2018 at +5.84 m, 2016 at +6.10 m, 1955 at +7.12 m, 1910 at +8.62 m) raises the 3D water surface and highlights flooded streets and buildings in real time.
* Metro and rail stations are plotted on the map and switch state as rising waters reach their elevation.
* Live impact counters track the flooded area in hectares, the number of affected buildings by arrondissement, and the number of flooded stations.
* Regulatory flood risk zones (PPRI / PHEC) can be toggled as an overlay to compare with the 3D water level.
* The map covers inner Paris (intra-muros), excluding the Bois de Boulogne and the Bois de Vincennes.

Available data sources (ODbL / Open Licence):

* Apur, "Emprise bâtie Paris" (footprint, height and median ground elevation of each building): https://carto2.apur.org/apur/rest/services/OPENDATA/EMPRISE_BATIE_PARIS/MapServer/0

prompts.description: Paris municipal tree canopy and remarkable trees biodiversity explorer
prompts.text:
Build an interactive map and biodiversity explorer of the municipal tree canopy of Paris.
The goal is an exceptional visual result, as clear, elegant and engaging as an environmental atlas or urban forestry dashboard, not a mere technical demo.
Expected result:

* An interactive map of Paris displays municipal trees with smooth spatial aggregation or clustering at high zooms and individual tree markers at close zooms, color-coded by botanical family/genus or height, with prominent visual badges for remarkable heritage trees (arbres remarquables).
* Interactive filters slice trees by arrondissement (1er to 20e), botanical genus/species (e.g., Platanus, Aesculus, Tilia, Sophora, Celtis), tree height and circumference ranges, and a one-click toggle for remarkable trees.
* An urban forest analytics panel provides summary metrics: total tree count, species and genus diversity breakdown (top species distribution chart), mean and median height/circumference, and canopy density by arrondissement.
* A remarkable trees showcase highlights Paris's heritage trees with their common name, scientific name, estimated planting date or age, remarkable criteria, and direct pan-to-map inspection.
* A district comparison view compares tree coverage across arrondissements, contrasting street trees against parks and public squares, with species variety indicators.
* Selecting any tree opens a detail card showing its exact location, French common name, botanical genus/species, height, circumference, and stage of development.

Available data sources (ODbL / Open Licence):

* Paris Open Data, "Les arbres" (municipal tree inventory with botanical name, height, circumference, address and coordinates): https://opendata.paris.fr/explore/dataset/les-arbres
* Paris Open Data, "Arbres remarquables" (heritage and remarkable trees of Paris with botanical data and history): https://opendata.paris.fr/explore/dataset/arbresremarquablesparis
* Paris Open Data, "Arrondissements" (Paris 20 administrative arrondissements boundaries): https://opendata.paris.fr/explore/dataset/arrondissements

prompts.description: Paris and Île-de-France Vélib real-time station availability and bike-share flow observatory
prompts.text:
Build an interactive live bike-share observatory and station availability explorer for the Vélib' Métropole network across Paris and Île-de-France.
The goal is an exceptional visual result, as responsive, clear and intuitive as a modern transit monitoring control room, not a mere technical demo.
Expected result:

* An interactive map of Greater Paris plots all active Vélib' stations, dynamically colored and styled by real-time status (empty, low availability, balanced, full) or by mechanical versus electric bike proportion.
* Instant search and multi-criteria filters let users filter by station name, commune or Paris arrondissement, minimum available mechanical bikes, minimum available electric bikes (e-bikes), and available return docks.
* A live network overview dashboard displays aggregate network metrics: total active stations, total operational bikes, mechanical vs. e-bike fleet share, global dock occupancy percentage, and critical shortage or surplus alerts.
* Interactive station inspection card opens on selection showing mechanical bikes, e-bikes, available empty docks, total capacity, and a visual fill-rate gauge.
* Territorial distribution analytics aggregate and rank bike availability, station density, and electric bike share across Paris arrondissements and neighboring Île-de-France municipalities.
* A toggle to inspect station status details (operational, closed, overflow) and quick shortcuts to highlight stations with high electric bike availability or available docks.

Available data sources (ODbL / Open Licence):

* Paris Open Data, "Vélib' - Disponibilité en temps réel des stations" (real-time station status, mechanical and e-bike counts, available docks, and coordinates): https://opendata.paris.fr/explore/dataset/velib-disponibilite-en-temps-reel
* Paris Open Data, "Vélib' - Emplacement des stations" (station locations, capacity, and terminal specifications): https://opendata.paris.fr/explore/dataset/velib-emplacement-des-stations
* transport.data.gouv.fr, "Vélib' Métropole GBFS" (official GBFS feeds for real-time station status and information): https://transport.data.gouv.fr/datasets/velib-metropole-donnees-temps-reel-gbfs
